we perform extensive RAI evaluations using publicly available benchmarks like BOLD

findings.text: Internal red teaming catalogued over 300 distinct attack techniques across languages and modalities, then fed failures back into model development.

source.quote:
In total, we identified and
developed over 300 distinct techniques (see Figure 4), and tested techniques individually and via chaining various
combinations.

findings.text: ActiveFence produced over 9,700 adversarial prompts across 20 categories for content- and security-targeted red teaming.

source.quote:
The team produced over 9,700 adversarial prompts, distributed over 20 categories, including content-targeted
red teaming

findings.text: Runtime input and output moderation models sit around the core model to catch jailbreaks, prompt injection, and RAI violations.

source.quote:
we built runtime input and output moderation models which serve as a first and
last line of defense and allow us to respond more quickly to newly identified threats or gaps in model alignment.

findings.text: Canvas and Reel outputs get an invisible watermark plus C2PA metadata, with a detection API planned soon after launch.

source.quote:
we incorporate an invisible watermark during the image or video generation
process and add C2PA9 metadata in all Canvas generated content.

notes: Technical report + model card (49 PDF pages). Safety numbers are sparse: BOLD, RealToxicityPrompts, and MM-SafetyBench are named with no scores; proprietary RAI benchmarks and red-teaming outcomes are qualitative. Included only BFCL v3 Hallucination/Irrelevance as a hallucination metric inside an otherwise agentic/tool-use table; skipped BFCL overall/AST/execution/relevance and all core capability, agentic, long-context, Canvas/Reel quality, and runtime tables. No Frontier Model Safety Framework thresholds or ASL-style risk decisions appear for these models. METR is a Controllability partnership only (not listed as a tester). Canvas and Reel are covered as rawModelName (not in seed). Seed-linked models Micro/Lite/Pro are covered; Nova Premier and Nova 2 are absent from this report.
